title: Nothing to teach (section 21)
hookLine: the Tathagata has no teaching to teach; that is called teaching

cards: A grandmother kneels on the kitchen floor, teaching a small child to tie a shoe. Two loops. Cross them.
Tuck one under. Pull. After a few tries the child gets it and beams.
Now, whose knot is that? The grandmother didn't invent it. Someone taught her, and someone taught them.
She's passing on something that was never hers, and the child will pass it on without ever saying her name.

teach.b: First, the instruction. Don't imagine, the Buddha tells Subhuti, that the Tathagata thinks, I have taught a teaching. Don't even form that idea.
Anyone who says the Tathagata has taught a teaching is misrepresenting him, the sutra says, and hasn't understood what he teaches.
That's startling: the voice that has taught all through this sutra refuses the title of the one who taught it. Third, the turn. Why?
Because as for teaching the teaching, there is no teaching to be found that could be taught; and that is what is called teaching the teaching. Set that beside a map. You'd be lost without one.

But a map isn't the place, and someone who keeps the map and never takes the trip has misunderstood what maps are for. The teaching, in this sutra, is never a possession handed from owner to owner. It's a pointing.
Fourth, the question behind. Then Subhuti asks something tender.
In ages to come, will there be beings who hear a teaching like this and trust it? The Buddha answers in the sutra's way: they are not beings, nor are they not beings.
The ones who will hear it can't be counted as fixed selves either.
The teaching passes through people the way a knot passes through hands. Nobody owns the knot, and yet every time it's tied right, a shoe stays on.
The Buddha teaches, fully and carefully, and lets go of owning what he taught.

how: Some Mahayana teachers frame their own teaching as pointing rather than possessing, and section 21 is read as the Buddha disowning any fixed teaching while still teaching.

practice: Bring to mind one thing you understand well, a recipe, a shortcut, a way of calming down, a fact you love, and remember who gave it to you, if you can.
Explain it in your head to a friend, slowly, and notice if a little pride rides along, the sense of it being yours. Let that soften, and finish the explanation as a messenger, not an owner.

wordCard.voice: Nothing to teach. Section twenty-one says there is no teaching to be found that could be taught, and that is called teaching. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the teaching, and also the way things are; Pali dhamma.

carryVoice: Your line: no teaching, teaching. The knot was never anyone's to keep. Until next time.
